facts.text: Hampton was originally called the Plantation of Winnacunnet and was one of four original New Hampshire townships chartered by Massachusetts.
The town was settled in 1638 by Reverend Stephen Bachiler, an Oxford graduate who had preached in Hampton, England.
The arrival of the railroad in 1840 changed Hampton forever, turning its oceanfront into a popular resort.
The Union House, later Hotel Whittier, was the first new uptown hotel, while the Leavitt and Nudd families ran beach inns that promoted Hampton Beach as vacation spot.
The library’s “New Hampshire Room” houses printed family genealogies, town histories, and genealogical periodicals, making it a key resource for local history.
In 1656, Eunice “Goody” Cole was convicted of witchcraft in Hampton and spent the rest of her life imprisoned in Boston, a rare case in New Hampshire.
